title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Verdant Analytics
next_steps: Redwood to send updated pricing addendum for 6 additional GPUs and two extra regions by 2026-07-05
SE to schedule 1-hour benchmark run with Verdant's test prompts on Redwood Dedicated (EU & APAC) week of 2026-07-12
Customer to confirm internal procurement timeline and target signature date (aiming for 2026-07-20)
Share SOC 2 + ISO docs and network diagram (Redwood) by 2026-07-03
action_items: Ravi Patel - Run perf test with Verdant testset on p4d equivalent + quantized profile - 2026-07-14
Maya Chen - Send pricing addendum and renewal paperwork for 12-month extension with expansion clause - 2026-07-05
Lena Ortiz - Prepare onboarding checklist and support SLA summary - 2026-07-06
Emily Carter - Share 3 representative production prompts and expected p95 latency SLAs - 2026-07-02
header: Date: 2026-07-01 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45 mins | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Emily Carter (Verdant Head of ML), Jason Lee (Verdant Infra Lead), Nora Chen (Verdant Procurement), Sam Ortiz (Verdant SRE)
summary: Quarterly renewal & expansion check-in. Customer is evaluating capacity upgrade (additional GPUs), adding EU and APAC regions, and a 12-month contract extension. Key open items: perf benchmark in additional regions, updated pricing addendum, SOC2/network docs, procurement timeline. Customer leans toward Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput but requested hosted fallback and cost comparison. Action items and next steps agreed.
topics: Pricing and cost vs hosted vs dedicated
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we wanted to run through the renewal and the expansion asks, i'll kick it off quick, hi emily hi jason hi nora
[00:12] Emily Carter: hey maya thanks, yeah appreciate it, we've been, you know, overall happy with the platform, traffic spiked last quarter and we're hitting close to our reserved capacity so want to talk through options
[00:28] Jason Lee: yeah we saw p95s creep up during batch jobs, and we'd like to add capacity and also bring inference closer to our EU customers, so two things: more GPUs and an EU region, maybe APAC later
[00:44] Ravi Patel: got it. quick clarifying q, are you running the same model replicas across regions or a regional routing policy?
[00:52] Emily Carter: right now same model replicas, but routing is geo based in our app layer; we were thinking maybe Redwood handle routing to nearest region for us to simplify things
[01:05] Maya Chen: that's doable; we can add region endpoints and set policy to route by latency. for dedicated we can reserve capacity in multiple regions, or use a hybrid - a primary dedicated cluster and hosted fallback.
[01:20] Nora Chen: procurement question — if we reserve dedicated GPUs in eu-west and ap-southeast, is that a separate contract or amend the existing one?
[01:30] Maya Chen: typically it's the same master subscription with an addendum for region capacity — i'll send an addendum that lays out the committed units per region and pricing, no separate legal entity needed.
[01:40] Sam Ortiz: any difference in encryption at rest or key mgmt if we go to dedicated in our VPC? we need KMS support and HSM for some regs
[01:49] Ravi Patel: dedicated in private mode supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; we also provide audit logs and per-token retention settings, we can show the network diagram.
[02:02] Emily Carter: perfect. and SOC2, iso? we need to give that to security
[02:08] Maya Chen: we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts; i'll share them as part of the security package.
[02:14] Jason Lee: about perf — we need p95 < 300 ms for the short prompts and under 1s for long context runs, are those realistic if we add 6 more GPUs?
[02:26] Ravi Patel: depends on model and sequence length; with the batching and kv cache we usually meet those p95s on dedicated for small to medium payloads. For long context we can use quantization profiles and kernel tuning. i'll propose a config: 6 gpus, mixed batch sizes, q4/qtune profile — we should run a benchmark with your prompt set to be sure
[02:46] Emily Carter: ok let's do the benchmark, we have a set of 200 representative prompts across short, medium, long, i'll share them after this call
[02:55] Maya Chen: great, and on pricing, we can propose two options: option A is a 12-month extension with committed capacity (lower unit cost), option B is a 6-month with optional rollover credits but higher unit price. for multi-region dedicated there is a small regional premium
[03:12] Nora Chen: procurement is leaning toward the 12-month if pricing is within X% of our current budget, we'll need final numbers to sign off. timeline wise we want to close by july 20th ideally
[03:25] Maya Chen: makes sense, we'll try to get the addendum and numbers to you by july 5th. that gives a two-week internal review window for you
[03:33] Jason Lee: one tech Q — can we do a canary traffic shift between regions, like warm up EU before sending production?
[03:39] Ravi Patel: yes, we support canary and gradual rollout policies per route; also automatic fallback to hosted if dedicated capacity is exhausted. caveat: cross-region cache warming might take a couple minutes depending on prefix reuse
[03:52] Emily Carter: are there any limits on model variants? we want to run a slightly-larger variant for certain critical requests and a quantized smaller variant for cost-sensitive flows
[04:02] Ravi Patel: supported — you can pin routes to model variants; runtime will route to variant A for policy X and variant B otherwise. automatic fallback if variant not available. we do recommend profiling quality with your eval set before you flip to cheaper variant
[04:19] Maya Chen: quick note, sometimes our docs refer to 'Redwood Dedicated' and some internal notes say 'Redwood Dedicate' — sorry for the typo in the doc, but it's the same product haha
[04:30] Emily Carter: haha noted
[04:33] Nora Chen: payment terms — will the expansion change invoicing cadence? we prefer net 45 for enterprise
[04:39] Maya Chen: payment terms can be updated in the addendum; net 45 is fine subject to legal review, i'll flag finance and legal to confirm
[04:48] Sam Ortiz: on compliance, one more thing — can we restrict logs to our account only and set token redaction? we have PHI in some prompts and want to limit exposure
[04:58] Ravi Patel: yes, we support per-account retention, token-level redaction and opt-out for training telemetry. for PHI we recommend private deployment with VPC and customer-managed keys which minimizes surface area
[05:12] Emily Carter: good, sounds like dedicated + VPC is the way. what's the delta cost vs hosted? give us a ballpark now
[05:20] Maya Chen: rough ballpark — hosted with on-demand throughput was costlier per token; dedicated with committed units typically drops unit cost by 30-40% depending on commitment. region premium for EU/APAC is about 8-12% per region. exact numbers in addendum though
[05:34] Jason Lee: we also need a runbook for failover, like if eu cluster loses nodes can traffic shift to na gracefully?
[05:41] Ravi Patel: yes, we can configure multi-tier fallback: EU dedicated -> NA dedicated -> Hosted. we emit tracing and a route-level fallback policy. i'll attach a sample runbook
[05:53] Emily Carter: great. on the benchmark, do you want us to provide raw logs or you can run with a dry dataset?
[05:59] Ravi Patel: best is your real prompts but anonymized; if that's hard, give us representative synthetic set with same token length distribution. we'll run the benchmark in EU and APAC and share p50/p95/p99 and throughput numbers
[06:13] Maya Chen: to set expectations, benchmarks will take a few days to schedule and run, then 24-48h to analyze; we'll put a margin for kernel tuning and quantization adjustments if needed
[06:24] Nora Chen: procurement needs an SKU line item for each region and committed GPU count to plug into our PO system
[06:30] Maya Chen: will include SKU lines in the addendum, yes
[06:33] Jason Lee: any limitations on model size or custom kernels? we use a custom attention optimization in house, wondering if we can bring a plugin
[06:42] Ravi Patel: currently we don't support external kernel plugins in hosted; for private deployments we can work with your infra team to integrate custom kernels but that is a professional services engagement. for Dedicated we can explore kernels if they're OSS and meet security checks
[06:58] Emily Carter: ok noted. one more item — SLOs for p95, do we have credits if SLOs breach?
[07:05] Lena Ortiz: for enterprise Dedicated we offer SLA credits tied to uptime and latency tiers; i'll include draft SLA language in the paperwork.
[07:13] Nora Chen: thanks lena. procurement will want a clear escalation path and contact list for incidents
[07:19] Lena Ortiz: we'll include that in the onboarding pack and support SLA doc
[07:24] Maya Chen: any other blockers?
[07:27] Emily Carter: just the benchmark and final pricing. if both look good procurement will push to sign by july 20
[07:33] Jason Lee: technical wise i'm good with the test matrix
[07:36] Sam Ortiz: same from SRE, want to see the runbook and trace retention settings
[07:41] Maya Chen: perfect. i'll recap next steps at the end. Ravi, are you ok to own the benchmark?
[07:47] Ravi Patel: yep i'll schedule infra and run EU/APAC on our side, need your prompt set and any gating scripts
[07:54] Emily Carter: i'll send the prompt set and gating script by tomorrow morning, anonymized
[07:58] Maya Chen: thank you. moving to recap — we will: 1) send pricing addendum with SKUs and payment terms by 2026-07-05; 2) SE to run dedicated benchmarks in EU & APAC week of 2026-07-12; 3) share SOC2/ISO docs and network diagram by 2026-07-03; 4) procurement aims to sign by 2026-07-20.
[08:21] Nora Chen: sounds good, appreciate the quick turnaround
[08:24] Maya Chen: great thank you everyone. we'll follow up in email and set the benchmark invite. bye
[08:29] Emily Carter: thanks all bye
[08:31] Jason Lee: bye
[08:33] (call ended)
